title: Catching Wrong Exception

bugs.explanation: `int('abc')` raises `ValueError`, not `TypeError`. Catching `TypeError` means the real exception propagates uncaught. Match the `except` clause to the actual exception type.

title: Bare Except Catches Everything

bugs.explanation: A bare `except:` catches every exception including `SystemExit`, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `GeneratorExit` — exceptions you almost never want to suppress. Always specify the exception type(s) you expect.

Multiple Except Clauses
try Without except or finally
code:
try:
    x = 1 / 0

bugs.explanation: A `try` block must have at least one `except` or `finally` clause. A lone `try:` without either is a `SyntaxError`.

title: assert With Message
Context Manager for File
code:
with open('data.txt', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
print(len(content))

title: File Read After Close
code:
f = open('data.txt')
f.close()
print(f.read())

bugs.explanation: Calling `f.read()` after `f.close()` raises `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file`. Use a `with` statement to ensure the file stays open during the read and is automatically closed afterwards.

title: Writing Mode Overwrites
code:
with open('log.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('entry 1\n')

with open('log.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write('entry 2\n')

bugs.explanation: Opening with `'w'` truncates the file each time. Opening twice with `'w'` erases 'entry 1'. Use `'a'` (append mode) on the second open to add entries without overwriting.

title: Encoding When Opening File
code:
with open('data.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    text = f.read()
print(text)

title: readlines vs readline
code:
with open('file.txt') as f:
    lines = f.readlines()
print(len(lines))

title: os.path.exists Before Opening
code:
import os
path = 'config.json'
if os.path.exists(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        print(f.read())
